findings.F1: The tested measure is on the side opposite to the idea. After large scaled rises in falling calm markets the coin rose instead of fading: the mean short-direction 3-day excess was -2.25 % (t -1.42, 62 cases on 46 days). The correlation of the forecast's size with the short-direction excess was -0.245. In folds B and C, 59 % of the 39 case bars had a positive 3-day excess, with a median of +1.2 %.
findings.F2: In folds B and C even the sign depends on how the cases are sampled, which marks it as noise. On all 38 case bars the long-direction excess was +3.1 % at 3 days (t 1.34), +3.5 % at 5 days (t 1.43) and +5.8 % at 10 days (37 bars, t 2.12). On the 3-day grid only 21 cases remain on 11 days, with -1.3 % long (pooled t -0.53). The 10-day grid holds 4 cases.
findings.F3: The move after a case is driven by a few coins and windows. XRP's 8 cases average +12.8 % at 3 days, and w14's 2 cases +45.4 %. The other coins sit near zero or mixed: ZEC -0.7 % on 10 cases, LTC -0.3 % on 7, ETH -0.6 % on 5. Years flip sign: 2018 +7.3 %, 2019 -2.6 %, 2020 +4.8 %, 2021 +5.2 %.
findings.F4: Among falling calm bars, the fade does not grow with the rise's size, so the idea's grading fails.
findings.F5: The weakness of falling calm markets is general, not specific to rise days.

no_ideas: The fade the theme claims is not in the data: large scaled rises in falling calm markets were followed by a rise, not a fall (-2.25 % short-direction, t -1.42, 62 cases). The giveback does not grow with the rise's size (correlation +0.038, or -0.245 on the forecast). The opposite move is too unstable across sampling, coins and years (F2, F3) to support an idea on another side.
